plan.topic: Orforglipron (Foundayo) and obstructive sleep apnea: the Phase 3 result presented at AHA 2026 and published in JAMA on Nov 9
plan.angle: 13:00 'what's confirmed?' Short. Sentence 1 (≤14 words): 'Orforglipron, the Foundayo pill, cut sleep apnea severity in two trials, but it isn't approved for that yet.' AHI in one line: breathing pauses per hour of sleep. Population: adults with moderate-to-severe OSA and overweight or obesity, two randomized trials vs placebo over 52 weeks, one without PAP and one with PAP. Give the average AHI change per arm in events per hour, taken from the JAMA paper, naming the dose arm (and how AHI was measured in the PAP trial). Status: not approved for sleep apnea; Lilly plans to file with the FDA, and filing isn't approval. Tirzepatide (Zepbound) is approved in the US for moderate-to-severe OSA in adults with obesity, from separate trials, not head-to-head. 'If you use CPAP, don't stop or change it on your own.' Then 'Not personal advice', the prescriber line, the Exp F line and the closing line. Title: 'Orforglipron (Foundayo) and Sleep Apnea: What's Confirmed? #shorts'.
plan.working_title: Orforglipron (Foundayo) Pill for Sleep Apnea: What's Confirmed? #shorts
plan.why: Spin-off of L1. A fresh randomized result on a drug people search for by name, with low competition. | fact-check: The result is real. ATTAIN-OSA was two Phase 3 RCTs (n=363 in adults not on PAP, n=349 in adults on PAP), 52 weeks, in adults with moderate-to-severe OSA and overweight or obesity. It was presented at AHA on 9 Nov 2026 and published in JAMA (Malhotra et al., doi:10.1001/jama.2026.24080). Healio reports AHI falling by about 18–21 events/hour on orforglipron vs 4–5 on placebo without PAP, and about 17–18 vs 5 with PAP. Source: https://www.healio.com/news/cardiology/20261109/oral-glp1-reduces-sleep-apnea-severity-improves-cardiometabolic-risk-factors. Lilly plans to file with the FDA by the end of 2026 (https://www.fiercepharma.com/pharma/lilly-heads-fda-phase-3-foundayo-win-sleep-apnea). Fixes: (1) The figures are ranges, which suggests more than one dose arm or estimand. The script must take one clearly named figure per arm from the JAMA paper (dose arm, estimand, and whether the PAP-group AHI was measured with PAP paused), not the press release's 'up to 44%'. Lead with events per hour vs placebo, with the percentage second if used at all. (2) Say 'two trials': one in people not using PAP, one in people using it. (3) Tirzepatide comparison: tirzepatide (Zepbound) is approved in the US for moderate-to-severe OSA in adults with obesity. That's obesity, not overweight, and tirzepatide is a GIP/GLP-1 medicine, so don't call it 'the GLP-1'. Separate trials, not head-to-head, no ranking. (4) The title 'Pill for Sleep Apnea' could read as approved. Use the 'What's Confirmed?' framing with the status by 6 s. (5) This counts as the week's single-trial Short.

Orforglipron (the Foundayo pill) cut sleep apnea severity compared with placebo in two 52-week Phase 3 trials in adults with moderate-to-severe obstructive sleep apnea and overweight or obesity. It isn't approved for sleep apnea. Lilly plans to file with the FDA, and filing isn't approval.
If you use CPAP, don't stop or change it on your own.
#orforglipron #SleepApnea #GLP1
Not personal advice. Talk to your doctor or prescriber about whether it's right for you.

factcheck.summary: The numbers and status claims check out against reachable sources. Healio's report of ATTAIN-OSA (JAMA, published 9 Nov 2026 with the AHA 2026 presentation) covers two 52-week placebo-controlled trials: 363 people not using PAP and 349 using it, all with moderate-to-severe OSA. Without PAP, AHI fell by 18–21 events an hour on orforglipron and 4–5 on placebo. With PAP, it fell by 17–18 versus 5. The JAMA record exists (PMID 43002161; Malhotra et al.). Fierce Pharma confirms that Lilly plans to file with the FDA by year's end and that Foundayo is currently approved only for weight management (April 2026). Zepbound's US approval for moderate-to-severe OSA in adults with obesity is correctly stated and correctly called separate trials, not head-to-head. Safety lines, the prescriber line and the Exp F and closing lines are all present. The script is 158 words, within the standard arm. There are no major problems. The minor fixes below keep the count at or under 160: say that the 18–21 range spans doses, drop the 'yet' that assumes approval, scope the stat cards and hook card, and swap the PubMed search URL for the direct record. One limit: I couldn't open the JAMA abstract (PubMed showed only a cookie wall), so the diabetes exclusion appears only in search-result summaries and the script doesn't claim it. I didn't add it.
